proposed_concrete: MOT-ATT-004 (proposed): brain-spine interface - ECoG decoding of attempted hip/knee/ankle movements in chronic spinal cord injury drives epidural electrical stimulation of the lumbosacral cord for walking (Lorach et al. 2023, doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06094-5)
reason: Replaces provisional class STM-SCS. The recorded signal is the cortical activity of attempted leg movement (MOT-ATT markers MK.SMR_ERD / MK.high_gamma from implanted ECoG); the spinal stimulation is the effector, not a stimulation-evoked brain marker, so by the class rule (same markers and construct) this is a MOT-ATT configuration, not a new stimulation class. New serial number by criterion 4 (continuous closed-loop control of stimulation producing real stepping) and criterion 1 (lower-limb joint classes). Suggest adding MK.high_gamma to the MOT-ATT class markers if accepted. bci_category active; recording ECoG; stimulus electrical_stimulation, motor_execution.

proposed_concrete: MOT-MI-012 (proposed): foot motor imagery brain switch triggering functional electrical stimulation of hand grasp in tetraplegia (Pfurtscheller et al. 2003, doi:10.1016/S0304-3940(03)00947-9)
reason: Replaces provisional class MOT-FES. Control signal is SMR ERD/ERS of foot motor imagery, the MOT-MI class marker; FES is the output and the feedback channel. Same class set as MOT-MI-004 (feet MI vs rest, beta rebound switch) but each detection advances the FES grasp sequence: criterion 4 (discrete feedback through FES-evoked movement instead of none). Note: this 2003 paper predates the first_source of MOT-MI-004 (2009) and should be noted there.

proposed_concrete: MOT-MI-0xx or MOT-ATT-0xx (proposed, maintainer to place): BCI-actuated FES for upper-limb rehabilitation after stroke - decoded movement intention of the paretic hand triggers FES of the hand/wrist extensors, compared with sham FES (Biasiucci et al. 2018, doi:10.1038/s41467-018-04673-z)
reason: Replaces provisional class MOT-FES. Same markers and construct as MOT-MI / MOT-ATT (SMR ERD of the intended movement); configuration differs by feedback (criterion 4: contingent FES producing real movement as rehabilitation feedback) and by the sham-FES control arm (criterion 1). The abstract does not say whether patients imagined or attempted the movement; place under MOT-ATT if the full text describes attempted movement. Related existing protocol: MOT-MRCP-003 (MRCP detection triggering peripheral nerve stimulation).

proposed_concrete: Variant on SSR-SSVEP-001 and on MOT-MI-001 (D-022 convention): "Hybrid: SSVEP + motor imagery (MOT-MI-001)" / "Hybrid: SSVEP + motor imagery (SSR-SSVEP-001)", source Allison et al. 2010 (doi:10.1088/1741-2560/7/2/026007)
reason: Replaces provisional class MOT-HYB. D-022 (confirmed) rules that hybrid BCIs are combinations of existing paradigms, not paradigms in their own right, and are recorded as 'Hybrid:' variants in each component paradigm; no new marker or construct is involved. Variants are written by the owner of the target paradigm (SSR-SSVEP: package B; MOT-MI: package B).

proposed_concrete: Variant on PER-ODD-001 and SSR-SSVEP-008 (D-022 convention): "Hybrid: P300 + SSVEP control-state detection (SSR-SSVEP-008)" / "Hybrid: P300 + SSVEP control-state detection (PER-ODD-001)", source Panicker et al. 2011 (doi:10.1109/TBME.2011.2116018)
reason: Replaces provisional class MOT-HYB (P300 + SSVEP example). Same D-022 reasoning. SSR-SSVEP-008 notes already mention this paper as a lead. PER-ODD is a package A paradigm, so the variant there is written by package A. Concept paper for the hybrid BCI: Pfurtscheller 2010 (doi:10.3389/fnpro.2010.00003; registry records list only the first author).
